Coffee Tuner — espresso dial-in rules

Read from the top. The first matching rule wins. Yield means the weight of espresso in the cup. Keep the dose fixed while comparing adjustments.

Roast profiles (ratio bounds, auto-flow time windows, temperature bands)
- Dark: starter ~1:1.7, bounds 1:1.4–1:2.1, auto-steady 18–35 s, 88–91 °C
- Medium: starter ~1:2.0, bounds 1:1.6–1:2.5, auto-steady 20–40 s (+4 s when ratio >= 1:2.4), 91–94 °C
- Light: starter ~1:2.5 (closer to 1:2.0 for heavy naturals), bounds 1:1.9–1:3.2, auto-steady 20–48 s, 93–96 °C

Priority rules
1. Uneven flow, or both sour and bitter: repeat with more even puck prep. Break up clumps, distribute to the edges, and tamp level. Keep dose, grind, yield, temperature, and pre-infusion fixed to isolate channeling.
2. Balanced taste (with fast, steady, or slow even flow): keep the recipe. Sensory balance overrides textbook clock targets, including fast 6-bar turbo shots and long-soak light roasts.
3. Slow or stalled flow with any remaining taste issue: try one small step coarser at the same target yield. Grinding past the puck's resistance peak clogs fine pathways, lowering bulk extraction (sour) while over-extracting narrow channels (bitter/dry).
4. Fast flow with sour or thin taste: try one small step finer at the same yield to add puck resistance, contact time, and body.
5. Fast flow with dry/astringent finish: repeat with even puck prep first. High-speed channels strip localized polyphenols; check distribution before touching grind.
6. Fast flow with bitter/harsh taste: shorten yield only if the ratio is already stretched past the roast starter (+0.15) or the coffee is a dark roast; otherwise check puck prep and sour–bitter confusion before shrinking a fast shot into a gusher.
7. Steady flow and sour, below the roast's max ratio: pull a slightly longer yield (~11% step, rounded to 0.5 g, minimum 2 g) to add solvent mass and lift extraction.
8. Steady flow and sour, at or above the roast's max ratio: keep yield fixed and move one micro-step finer (or raise temperature later) instead of diluting the cup further.
9. Steady flow and bitter/harsh, above the roast's min ratio: stop the shot a little earlier (~11% step, rounded to 0.5 g, minimum 2 g) to cut late-extracting bitter compounds and boost concentration.
10. Steady flow and bitter/harsh, at or below the roast's min ratio: keep yield fixed and move one micro-step coarser (or lower temperature later) instead of shrinking the drink further.
11. Steady flow and dry/astringent: shorten yield if the ratio is stretched (> starter + 0.3); otherwise repeat with even puck prep, and step one notch coarser on the next shot if dryness persists.
12. Flavor balanced, body too thin or too heavy: shorten yield for fuller body (or step finer at the min ratio floor); lengthen yield for a lighter, more open cup (or step coarser at the max ratio ceiling).

Yield steps and overshoot bisection
Coffee Tuner uses an ~11% yield trial rounded to the nearest 0.5 g (minimum 2 g move) to match the +/- 0.5 g UI steppers—for example, 36 g -> 40 g longer or 32 g shorter, and 45 g -> 50 g longer or 40 g shorter. When a user applies a yield change and the next shot flips from sour straight to bitter (or vice versa), the app suggests splitting the difference halfway between the two yields.

Shot time and temperature
Measure time from pump or lever start to target yield, including pre-infusion. Manual flow selection overrides automatic time classification. Brew temperature is optional; when entered within a roast's adjustable range during steady flow, the app offers a +/- 1 °C follow-up suggestion if yield changes alone leave a shot sour or bitter.
